column4: ### Defining Faith
column5: ### Definition of Faith

column4: Faith is a commonly misunderstood and misrepresented aspect of Christianity. As the saying goes, “there is a ditch on both sides of the road”! Because the word faith is so commonly used without proper explanation in our modern Christianity, it can come to pick up erroneous definitions amplified through misunderstanding. Faith is often portrayed either as a blanketed statement of abstracted belief or as an almost mystical power or “magic,” something you possess in a specific measured and limited amount.
column5: Faith is a commonly misunderstood and misrepresented aspect of Christianity. As the saying goes, “there’s a ditch on both sides of the road”! Because in modern Christianity the word faith is often used without proper explanation, it can take on misdefinitions amplified by misunderstandings. Faith is often presented either as a general, abstract statement of belief, or as almost a mystical force or “magic,” something you possess in a specific, measured, and limited amount.

column4: #### What Faith is Not
column5: #### What Faith Is Not

column4: Faith misrepresented abstractly has no specific conviction or persuasion. This is often evident with a bit of probing as this representation of faith cannot be made specific. If you ask, ‘what do you believe’ or ‘why do you believe’ the person with this understanding of faith often cannot clarify beyond ‘I believe’. 1 Peter 3:15 says we should be ready to give an answer for the hope that is in us.
column5: When faith is presented as abstract, it has no specific conviction or persuasion. A little probing makes this clear, because this representation of faith cannot become specific. If you ask, ‘What do you believe?’ or ‘Why do you believe?’ the person with this understanding of faith often cannot explain beyond ‘I believe.’ 1 Peter 3:15 says that we should be ready to give an answer about the hope that is in us.

column4: Sometimes people think of faith like a magical power-but that’s not what Scripture teaches. Faith is about a real relationship built on trust. In Scripture, faith is far more dynamic and relational-it’s rooted in persuasion, trust, and confidence in God’s character and promises. It’s not an impersonal force but an engaged response to God that shapes thoughts, feelings, and actions.

column4: #### Faith is Persuasion
column5: #### Faith Is Persuasion

column4: So, what is faith? Persuasion! The Greek word ***pistis*** means persuasion, or the result of being persuaded. We are to have persuasion towards God. In English we might say faith (persuasion) ‘**in** God’. If you are married, you hopefully have faith ‘**in’** your spouse. You believe that they will do what they said they would do, and you believe that they are being authentic and genuine. This trust should extend beyond what they’ve said, to extend to them in general.
column5: So, what is faith? Being persuaded! The Greek word ***pistis*** means being persuaded, or the result of being persuaded. We are to be persuaded about God. In English we might say: faith (persuasion) ‘**in** God’. If you are married, then hopefully you have faith ‘**in’** your spouse. You believe that they will do what they said they would do, and you also believe that they are sincere and genuine. This trust should go beyond the things they have said and extend, more generally, to their very person.

column4: Developing faith, persuasion, and trust in a relationship takes time and experience. Hopefully in life you have learned how to develop a trusting relationship with another person. The principles you’ve learned that allow you to increase your trust in someone you know will also allow you can increase your faith in God. Faith in a relationship is increased over time, in experience, with consistency, and through small and large actions that build your confidence in the other person’s character and nature.

In a relationship, faith grows over time, through experience, with consistency, and through small and large actions that build your confidence in the other person’s character and nature.

column4: ‘Faith towards God’, is relational. Relationships are built by two parties, not one. The good news about our faith in God is that God is responsible for His side of the relationship (made possible by the atoning death of Jesus, and the infilling of His spirit at rebirth), and He helps us on our side too (through the work of the Comforter - the Holy Spirit). God is doing almost all the work, our part (as we will discuss later in this chapter) is to walk *WITH* Him in obedience.
column5: ‘Faith toward God’ is relational. Relationships are made of two parties, not one. God is doing almost all the work; our part (as we will explain further in this chapter) is to walk (*WITH*) with Him in obedience.

column4: ### Jesus Matures Our Faith
column5: ### Jesus perfects our faith

column4: Jesus is the author and perfecter of our faith (Hebrews 12:2). Our faith is designed to be continually growing and expanding. We don’t reach a single point where we have enough ‘faith’, but rather our faith increases. Consider a deep and personal relationship you have in your life today. As in any relationship we don't arrive at a specific milestone where now we ‘know’ the person. We continue to know them, and increase our knowledge of them, and this refines, shapes, and grows our relationship.
column5: Jesus is the author and finisher of our faith (Hebrews 12:2). Our faith is designed to keep growing and expanding continually. We do not arrive at a point where we have enough ‘faith’; rather, our faith keeps increasing. Consider a deep and personal relationship in your life. As with any relationship, we do not reach a specific milestone at which we have now ‘known’ the person. We keep on knowing them, increase our familiarity with them, and this process refines, shapes, and grows our relationship.

column4: How do we grow our faith in God? By continuing to experience Him across His many revelations, manifestations, and attributes. Again, consider a deep personal relationship in your life. You increase the depth of relationship by engaging them in different ways, in different formats, in different mediums, in different settings. You talk to them, message them, perhaps write to them. You see them individually, and in group settings. You talk about what you value, and perhaps you challenge one another. The numerous ways go on to infinity. Across these many expressions you come to know the person more deeply.

column4: There are two Greek words for ‘Word’ in the Bible-**logos** and **rhema**. Understanding the difference helps us see how faith grows.
column5: There are two Greek words for ‘word’ in the Bible—**logos** and **rhema**. Understanding their difference shows us how faith grows.

column4: **Logos**: generally, refers to the **concept, idea, reason, or broader expression of God’s word**. It encompasses a universal, foundational truth or message and is often used to describe God’s eternal wisdom and Christ Himself as the living Word.
column5: **Logos**: Generally points to the **concept, idea, logic, or broader expression** of God’s word. It encompasses a universal, fundamental truth or message and is often used to describe God’s eternal wisdom and Christ Himself as the living Word.

column4: **Rhema (G4487)**: emphasizes a **specific, spoken word or utterance**. It typically refers to a particular word or message given in a specific moment, especially a spoken or revealed word that applies directly to a person’s situation.
column5: **Rhema (G4487)**: Emphasizes a specific, spoken word or utterance. It generally points to a particular word or message given at a particular moment, especially speech or a revealed word that applies directly to a person’s situation.

column4: *Logos* is like the entire message of a book, whereas *rhema* is like a particular passage or sentence that speaks directly to someone at a given moment. While *logos* is God’s overarching truth, *rhema* is when part of that truth is spoken to an individual in a personal, applicable way. Together, they illustrate the fullness of God’s communication: *logos* as the broad, foundational truths of God’s character and will, and *rhema* as the specific, applied word that brings that truth alive in a person’s life and situation.
column5: *Logos* is like the entire message of a book, whereas *Rhema* is like a specific passage or sentence that directly addresses someone at a particular moment. While *Logos* is God’s all-encompassing truth, *Rhema* is the moment when a portion of that truth is spoken to an individual in a personal and applicable way. Together, they present a picture of the full comprehensiveness of God’s communication: *Logos* the broad, foundational truths of God’s character and will, and *Rhema* the specific, operative word that brings that truth to life in a person’s life and circumstances.

column4: ### Example of a Rhema Word in Action
column5: ### Example of the Rhema Word in Action

column4: God promises revelation and wisdom for all those that ask. When He speaks to us, that utterance is a *rhema* word. Rhema words are from God and serve to confirm, lead, and guide us. They are not a replacement for the *logos* word, nor do they carry authority of scripture. *Rhema* words are to be judged by the same standard as prophecy or interpretation of tongues (see the chapter on the Holy Spirit for an in-depth study on this topic).
column5: God promises revelation and wisdom to all who ask. When He speaks to us, that utterance is a *Rhema* word. A Rhema word is from God and serves to give us confirmation, direction, and guidance. It is not a substitute for the *Logos* word, nor does it carry the authority of Scripture. A *Rhema* word should be tested by the same standard by which prophecy or the interpretation of tongues is tested (see the chapter on the Holy Spirit for an in-depth study on this topic).

column4: At several points in my career, I have prayed for divine guidance. Several years ago, I was contemplating the process of starting to look for a new opportunity and in my prayer time, I heard God say to me ‘*Just wait on me, I have an opportunity for you.’* I was starting to look for a new job because I was dissatisfied with my current role and felt frustrated. God’s word of direction ‘*wait on me’* helped me have peace and confidence in an otherwise restless season.
column5: At several points in my career, I have prayed for divine guidance. God’s instruction, ‘*Wait for Me*,’ gave me peace and confidence in a restless season.

column4: Three of four months passed, I kept working hard and faithfully, keeping my attitude positive. God would remind me, *‘wait on me’*, then His promise occurred. I had an opportunity to be promoted and received a generous wage increase.
column5: Three or four months went by; I continued to work diligently and faithfully and kept my attitude positive. God would remind me, *‘Wait for Me’*, then His promise was fulfilled. I received a promotion opportunity and a generous increase in pay.

column4: I could have continued my job search; I could have left. I could have started somewhere new. No doubt someone else would have gotten that promotion! But because I sought the Lord’s counsel and was persuaded in His **rhema word**, I obeyed, and received the benefit. God’s words are **alive and personal**, and He promises to give us manifold and liberal wisdom (James 1:5).

column4: I have dozens if not hundreds of times where I have prayed and asked God what to do and He has given me a rhema word. Not each had the same spectacular outcome, but they all brought a sense of peace and confidence that I was obeying God and that He would work things out. They were the words I needed for the moment! column4: When Jesus appeared to His disciples and calmed them down (I imagine it's quite alarming when someone appears in your midst, having come through locked doors), He spoke to Thomas. He did not criticize or blame Thomas or accuse him as part of the wicked and perverse generation seeking a sign (Matthew 16:4) but revealed Himself to Thomas.

column4: Jesus goes on to say, ‘*blessed are they who have not seen and have believe*d’. This is not Jesus encouraging ‘blind or ignorant faith’ or rejecting the use of empirical evidence. But He is saying that we are more blessed when we can believe without the need for empirical proof. Why? If our faith, our trust, was limited to purely what we had seen empirically demonstrated, we could never have any confidence in the future work. We would have great confidence in what had been accomplished but would not walk in the peace of God for our tomorrows and for our future.

column5: Beyond basic relational skills, there are certain practices and disciplines that will strengthen your relationship with God:

column4: - **Build and Maintain a Prayer Life, Listen and Communicate with God.** Regular, heartfelt prayer is essential to a close relationship with God. Through prayer, you can share your worries, joys, and gratitude, seeking His guidance and strength. (*Philippians 4:6-7*) Being sensitive to the Holy Spirit’s voice helps you discern God’s will, find wisdom in decisions, and grow in spiritual maturity. Take time for quiet reflection to hear His direction. (*Romans 8:14*)
column5: - **Establish and maintain a life of prayer; listen to God and converse with Him.** Regular, heartfelt prayer is essential for a close relationship with God. Through prayer you can express your concerns, joys, and thanksgiving, and seek His guidance and strength. (*Philippians 4:6-7*) Remaining sensitive to the voice of the Holy Spirit helps you discern God’s will, gain wisdom in decisions, and grow in spiritual maturity. Set aside quiet time for reflection to listen for His guidance. (*Romans 8:14*)

column4: - **Spend Time in Worship.** Worship is a powerful way to draw close to God, expressing love and reverence. Through praise, song, or quiet reflection, worship deepens your awareness of His presence. (*Psalms 100:2-4*)

column4: - **Read, Study, and Meditate on Scripture.** God’s Word reveals His character, promises, and instructions for life. Dedicating time to studying Scripture helps you grow in faith, understanding, and spiritual resilience. (*2 Timothy 3:16-17*)
column5: - **Read, study, and meditate on Scripture.** God’s Word reveals His character, promises, and instructions for life. Setting aside time to study the Word helps you grow in faith, understanding, and spiritual steadfastness. (*2 Timothy 3:16-17*)

column4: - **Obey His Commandments.** Obedience to God’s instructions demonstrates your love, respect, and trust in Him. Walking in obedience aligns your life with His purpose and brings blessings. (*John 14:15*)

column4: - **Actively Attend a Local Church and Serve.** Engaging in a church community offers spiritual support, encouragement, and opportunities to serve others. Being involved helps build a sense of belonging and strengthens your commitment to God’s mission. (*Hebrews 10:24-25*)
column5: - **Participate actively in and serve your local church.** Being part of the church community provides spiritual support, encouragement, and opportunities to serve others. Staying engaged strengthens your sense of belonging and your commitment to God’s mission. (*Hebrews 10:24-25*)

column4: - **Build Relationships with Other Believers.** Fellowship with other Christians provides accountability, encouragement, and shared wisdom. These relationships enrich your faith journey and help you grow through mutual support. (*Proverbs 27:17*)

column4: Our ‘faith towards God’ is not a one-time occurrence for salvation but is an ongoing practice and relationship that we are supposed to cultivate our entire lives. The benefits of a trusting and beneficial relationship are incredibly numerous, but we must do the good work of fostering that trust and growth to see it thrive.
